### Atlas and local surrogates can replace the individual connectome {#sec-annex-s1-surrogates}

Full results of the surrogate connectomes summarized in @sec-s1-surrogates.

#### CSET with Surrogate Connectomes {#sec-annex-surrogate-cset}

```{python filename="simf_surrogate_full_stats.py"}
#| output: false
import mindmap as mm

# self-contained, like the other "Full Results" Annex sections above -
# reloads and recomputes independently of the main-text surrogate cell
# rather than reusing its variables (same identical calls, disk-cache hit).
surrogates_full = ["beltrami", "fused", "fused-bin", "geom-atlas", "geom-atlas-bin"]
conditions_full = ["original"] + surrogates_full

# same reader-facing renaming as the main-text cell (index.qmd, surrogate section) - fused/
# fused-bin/geom-atlas/geom-atlas-bin are the on-disk `Surrogate` tags.
SURROGATE_LABELS_FULL = {
    "beltrami": "Beltrami (GBF)", "fused": "atlas", "fused-bin": "atlas-bin",
    "geom-atlas": "local", "geom-atlas-bin": "local-bin",
}

surr_metrics_full = mm.metric.MetricSuite.load("../results/simf/surrogates")
surr_comparisons_full = surr_metrics_full.stat.build_comparisons(["original"], surrogates_full)

# Margins, as in the main text (index.qmd): 5 mm for localization error, 0.1 for spatial correlation.
DELTA_FULL = {"localization_error": 5.0, "correlation": 0.1}
HIGHER_IS_BETTER_FULL = {"localization_error": False, "correlation": True}

def _surr_margin_tests(metric, method, phase):
    """Surrogate vs. original, region-paired, ties kept (Pratt): the two-sided Wilcoxon for the Hodges-Lehmann
    shift and rank-biserial r (99% CIs), and one-sided Wilcoxons against ±δ, Holm across the five surrogates
    within each direction, as in the main text. "original" is the reference, so the metric's direction is
    flipped to read "better" as "surrogate better"."""
    return margin_tests(
        surr_metrics_full.stat.wilcoxon, metric, delta=DELTA_FULL[metric], reference="original",
        higher_is_better=not HIGHER_IS_BETTER_FULL[metric], group_by="Surrogate", comparisons=surr_comparisons_full,
        pairing_col="region", filters={"Method": method, "phase": phase}, correction="holm", zero_method="pratt",
        effect_sizes=("hodges_lehmann", "rank_biserial"), ci_seed=0, ci_level=CI_LEVEL,
    )

# CSET's own breakdown - wCSET's is reported in full in the main text.
surr_loc_cset_tests = _surr_margin_tests("localization_error", "cset", "qrp")
surr_corr_cset_tests = {phase: _surr_margin_tests("correlation", "cset", phase) for phase in ["qrp", "pp"]}
surr_loc_cset = surr_loc_cset_tests["base"]
surr_corr_cset = {phase: t["base"] for phase, t in surr_corr_cset_tests.items()}

# statistics quoted in the prose below: "better"/"worse" = surrogate better/worse by more than the margin.
_loc_cset_v = margin_verdicts(surr_loc_cset_tests)
_corr_cset_v = {ph: margin_verdicts(t) for ph, t in surr_corr_cset_tests.items()}
_loc_cset = surr_loc_cset.vs("original", higher_is_better=False)  # positive = surrogate better (lower error)
loc_cset_hl = {s: fmt_ci(_loc_cset.loc[s], "hodges_lehmann", unit=" mm", level=CI_LEVEL) for s in surrogates_full}
loc_cset_p = {s: fmt_p(_loc_cset_v.loc[s, "p_corrected"]) for s in surrogates_full}
_others = [s for s in surrogates_full if s != "beltrami"]
loc_cset_others_p_min = fmt_p(_loc_cset_v.loc[_others, "p_corrected"].min())
corr_cset_p_min = fmt_p(min(v["p_corrected"].min() for v in _corr_cset_v.values()))
_corr_cset_hl = [surr_corr_cset[ph].vs("original", higher_is_better=False)["hodges_lehmann"] for ph in ["qrp", "pp"]]
corr_cset_lo = fmt_num(min(-h.max() for h in _corr_cset_hl), 2)
corr_cset_hi = fmt_num(max(-h.min() for h in _corr_cset_hl), 2)

# wCSET's spatial correlation at the quarter rising phase (the main text shows the peak only).
surr_corr_wcset_qrp_tests = _surr_margin_tests("correlation", "wcset", "qrp")
surr_corr_wcset_qrp = surr_corr_wcset_qrp_tests["base"]

# dSPM's and sLORETA's benchmark reference lines, as in the main text: solved in the surrogate run on the same
# samples (Surrogate="none") and summarized like the boxes they are drawn over: mean over repetitions per region,
# median across regions.
_ref_methods_full = ["dspm", "sloreta"]
def _surr_ref_full(metric, phase):
    df = surr_metrics_full.to_df(metrics=metric, filters={"Surrogate": "none", "phase": phase, "Method": _ref_methods_full})
    return df.groupby(["Method", "region"])["Value"].mean().groupby("Method").median().to_dict()
surr_ref_loc_full = _surr_ref_full("localization_error", "qrp")
surr_ref_corr_full = {phase: _surr_ref_full("correlation", phase) for phase in ["qrp", "pp"]}
```

This section reports CSET's full surrogate-connectome breakdown (@fig-annex-surrogate-cset), summarized qualitatively in the main text alongside wCSET's own (@sec-s1-surrogates), which is reported there in full.

As in the main text, the tests ask whether a surrogate changed the outcome by more than the margin (5 mm, or 0.1 in correlation), in either direction (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests against ±δ, region-paired, Holm-corrected across the five surrogates within each direction).

For localization error, only the Laplace-Beltrami surrogate (GBF) changed CSET's accuracy by significantly more than the margin: it worsened it by `{python} loc_cset_hl['beltrami']` (p_corrected `{python} loc_cset_p['beltrami']`). With the atlas, atlas-bin, local and local-bin surrogates, no difference significantly exceeded the margin in either direction (smallest p_corrected `{python} loc_cset_others_p_min`).

For spatial correlation, CSET was slightly lower with every surrogate, by Δr = `{python} corr_cset_lo`–`{python} corr_cset_hi` at the two phases, and no difference significantly exceeded the 0.1 margin (smallest p_corrected `{python} corr_cset_p_min`).

```{python filename="simf_surrogate_cset_plot.py"}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-annex-surrogate-cset
#| fig-cap: "CSET accuracy using the true structural connectome versus five dMRI-free connectome surrogates (a–c: box = IQR, line = median). (a) Localization error (mm) at the quarter rising phase. (b, c) Spatial correlation with ground truth at the quarter rising phase (b) and peak phase (c). Dashed lines mark dSPM's and sLORETA's values as connectome-free benchmarks, summarized like the boxes (mean over repetitions per region, median across regions). (d–f) Paired difference vs. the original connectome, one value per region (mean over repetitions; violin = distribution, thick line = median, thin line = IQR), positive = surrogate better; dashed lines = margin δ = ±5 mm or ±0.1. Above each violin: ▲/▼ = surrogate better/worse than the original connectome by more than δ (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test against ±δ, region-paired, Holm-corrected across the five surrogates within each direction; \\*p<0.05, \\*\\*p<0.01, \\*\\*\\*p<0.001), ns = neither; rank-biserial r (positive = surrogate better) and the number of regions where the surrogate is better/tied/worse. wCSET's equivalent comparisons are reported in @fig-surrogate."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

CONDITION_COLORS_FULL = {
    "original": LINE_COLOR,
    "beltrami": "#2a78d6",
    "fused": "#eb6834",
    "fused-bin": "#1baf7a",
    "geom-atlas": "#eda100",
    "geom-atlas-bin": "#e87ba4",
}

ref_methods_full = ["dspm", "sloreta"]
phase_titles_full = {"qrp": "Quarter rising phase", "pp": "Peak phase"}
panel_letters_full = {"loc": "a", "qrp": "b", "pp": "c"}

def surr_box_panel(metric, method, phase, ax, ref_medians):
    """Boxes per connectome condition (descriptive only: the tests are in the paired panels), dSPM/sLORETA
    medians as dashed lines."""
    surr_metrics_full.plot.box(
        metric, "Surrogate", unit="region", filters={"Method": method, "phase": phase}, order=conditions_full,
        palette=CONDITION_COLORS_FULL, points=False, fill_alpha=FILL_ALPHA, labels=SURROGATE_LABELS_FULL, ax=ax,
        rotate_ticks=45,
    )
    for m in ref_methods_full:
        ax.axhline(ref_medians[m], color=COLORS[m], linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, zorder=0.5,
                   label=f"{METHOD_LABELS[m]} (benchmark)")
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

surr_cset_fig, (surr_cset_axes, surr_cset_daxes) = plt.subplots(
    2, 3, figsize=(len(conditions_full) * 1.3 * 2.4, 10.5), gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.6})

_cset_panels = [
    ("loc", "localization_error", "qrp", surr_ref_loc_full, surr_loc_cset_tests, "Localization error (mm)",
     "Original − surrogate (mm)", "Localization error\n(quarter rising phase)"),
    ("qrp", "correlation", "qrp", surr_ref_corr_full["qrp"], surr_corr_cset_tests["qrp"], "Spatial correlation",
     "Surrogate − original (r)", phase_titles_full["qrp"]),
    ("pp", "correlation", "pp", surr_ref_corr_full["pp"], surr_corr_cset_tests["pp"], "Spatial correlation",
     "Surrogate − original (r)", phase_titles_full["pp"]),
]
for i, (key, metric, phase, ref, tests, ylabel, dylabel, title) in enumerate(_cset_panels):
    ax, dax = surr_cset_axes[i], surr_cset_daxes[i]
    surr_box_panel(metric, "cset", phase, ax, ref)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(f"{panel_letters_full[key]}. {title}")
    if metric == "correlation":
        ax.set_ylim(0, 0.9)
    # Stars: surrogate better (▲) / worse (▼) by more than the margin, dashed lines at ±δ
    paired_margin_plot(
        surr_metrics_full, tests, order=surrogates_full, ax=dax, palette=CONDITION_COLORS_FULL,
        labels=SURROGATE_LABELS_FULL, rotate_ticks=45,
        direction_labels=("surrogate better", "original better") if i == len(_cset_panels) - 1 else None,
    )
    dax.set_ylabel(dylabel)
    dax.set_title(f"{'def'[i]}. Paired difference vs. original")

surr_cset_fig.legend(*surr_cset_axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02))

plt.tight_layout()
```

The main text reports wCSET's spatial correlation at the peak (@fig-surrogate). At the quarter rising phase, before activity spreads, the surrogates' effects were small (@fig-annex-surrogate-early).

```{python filename="simf_surrogate_wcset_qrp_plot.py"}
surr_qrp_fig, (surr_qrp_ax, surr_qrp_dax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(len(conditions_full) * 1.3 * 1.8, 5.5))

    direction_labels=("surrogate better", "original better"), rotate_ticks=45,
)
surr_qrp_dax.set_ylabel("Surrogate − original\n(spatial correlation)")
surr_qrp_dax.set_title("b. Paired difference vs. original", loc="left", fontsize=10)

surr_qrp_fig.legend(*surr_qrp_ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="lower center", ncol=2, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.06))
plt.tight_layout()
```

### Prior Similarity of Surrogate and Perturbed Connectomes {#sec-annex-prior-sim}

```{python filename="simf_prior_similarity_stats.py"}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Similarities computed by processing_simf.qmd ("Prior Similarity"): the individual prior against each perturbed
# connectome and each surrogate, with every harmonic ("similarity") and without the λ = 0 harmonics
# ("similarity_nonzero"), plus each connectome's smallest nonzero eigenvalue and the share of its prior held by the
# λ = 0 harmonics.
prior_sim = pd.read_csv("../results/simf/prior_similarity/similarity.csv")
_pert = prior_sim[prior_sim["kind"] == "perturbation"].set_index("percentage").sort_index()
_surr = prior_sim[prior_sim["kind"] == "surrogate"].set_index("connectome")
PRIOR_SIM_VERSIONS = ["similarity", "similarity_nonzero"]

# Equivalent perturbation: the share of swapped edges at which the perturbation curve reaches the surrogate's
# similarity, by linear interpolation between the tested levels. Both curves decrease monotonically.
prior_sim_equiv = pd.DataFrame({
    col: np.interp(-_surr[col], -_pert[col].to_numpy(), _pert.index.to_numpy()) for col in PRIOR_SIM_VERSIONS
}, index=_surr.index)

# The surrogates split into the same two groups in both versions: atlas and the two local surrogates are closest
# to the individual prior, atlas-bin and GBF further away.
prior_sim_close, prior_sim_far = ["fused", "geom-atlas", "geom-atlas-bin"], ["fused-bin", "beltrami"]

def _range(values, digits, scale=1):
    lo, hi = fmt_num(min(values) * scale, digits), fmt_num(max(values) * scale, digits)
    return lo if lo == hi else f"{lo}–{hi}"

def _sim(col, pct):
    return fmt_num(_pert.loc[pct, col], 2)

ps_all, ps_nz = "similarity", "similarity_nonzero"
# curves: with every harmonic, the similarity falls fast and levels off; without λ = 0, it falls slowly, then to ~0
ps_all_10, ps_all_30, ps_all_100 = _sim(ps_all, 10), _sim(ps_all, 30), _sim(ps_all, 100)
ps_nz_40, ps_nz_70, ps_nz_100 = _sim(ps_nz, 40), _sim(ps_nz, 70), _sim(ps_nz, 100)

# mechanism: swaps open a spectral gap, pushing the prior's weight onto the λ = 0 harmonic
ps_lambda_orig = fmt_num(_pert.loc[0, "lambda_min_nonzero"], 3)
ps_lambda_10, ps_lambda_50 = fmt_num(_pert.loc[10, "lambda_min_nonzero"], 2), fmt_num(_pert.loc[50, "lambda_min_nonzero"], 2)
ps_share_orig = fmt_num(_pert.loc[0, "zero_share"] * 100, 0)
ps_share_10, ps_share_30 = fmt_num(_pert.loc[10, "zero_share"] * 100, 0), fmt_num(_pert.loc[30, "zero_share"] * 100, 0)
ps_share_50 = fmt_num(_pert.loc[50, "zero_share"] * 100, 1)
ps_share_graph = _range(_surr.loc[["fused", "fused-bin", "geom-atlas", "geom-atlas-bin"], "zero_share"], 0, 100)
ps_share_gbf = fmt_num(_surr.loc["beltrami", "zero_share"] * 100, 0)
ps_floor = fmt_num(np.sqrt(_pert.loc[0, "zero_share"]), 2)  # the λ = 0 harmonic's contribution alone: 1 / ‖w₀²‖

# surrogates: similarities and equivalent perturbation per version and group
ps_close_all, ps_close_nz = _range(_surr.loc[prior_sim_close, ps_all], 2), _range(_surr.loc[prior_sim_close, ps_nz], 2)
ps_far_all, ps_far_nz = _range(_surr.loc[prior_sim_far, ps_all], 2), _range(_surr.loc[prior_sim_far, ps_nz], 2)
ps_close_all_eq, ps_close_nz_eq = _range(prior_sim_equiv.loc[prior_sim_close, ps_all], 0), _range(prior_sim_equiv.loc[prior_sim_close, ps_nz], 0)
ps_far_all_eq, ps_far_nz_eq = _range(prior_sim_equiv.loc[prior_sim_far, ps_all], 0), _range(prior_sim_equiv.loc[prior_sim_far, ps_nz], 0)
ps_eq_min, ps_eq_max = fmt_num(prior_sim_equiv.to_numpy().min(), 0), fmt_num(prior_sim_equiv.to_numpy().max(), 0)

# where those levels fall in the perturbation experiment (the degradation tests reloaded above): wCSET's correlation
# advantage over both references, and its localization advantage over sLORETA
def _better_end(metric, refs):
    ends = []
    for ref in refs:
        cl = deg_results[metric].clusters_by_pair[(ref, "wcset")]
        cl = cl[cl["significant"].astype(bool) & (cl["sign"] < 0)]
        ends.append(cl["percentage_end"].iloc[0])
    return min(ends)

def _worse_start(metric, ref):
    cl = deg_results[metric].clusters_by_pair[(ref, "wcset")]
    cl = cl[cl["significant"].astype(bool) & (cl["sign"] > 0)]
    return cl["percentage_start"].iloc[0]

ps_corr_end = fmt_num(_better_end("correlation", DEG_REFERENCES), 0)
ps_loc_end = fmt_num(_better_end("localization_error", ["sloreta"]), 0)
ps_loc_worse = fmt_num(_worse_start("localization_error", "sloreta"), 0)
```

The perturbation experiment (@sec-s1-prior-noise) measures connectome errors as a share of swapped edges, which has no equivalent for the surrogates (@sec-s1-surrogates): they differ from the individual connectome in edge count, weights and topology at once. To place them on the same scale, we compared the priors themselves. wCSET uses a connectome only through its prior covariance, Σ = U diag(w²) Uᵀ, with U the connectome's harmonics and w their weights (the low-pass exp(−5λ) for connectome harmonics and GBF's log-decay with a cutoff of 150 for the geometric ones, as in the runs). We measured the similarity of two priors as the cosine similarity of their covariance matrices, sim(Σ₁, Σ₂) = Σᵢⱼ w₁ᵢ² w₂ⱼ² (u₁ᵢ · u₂ⱼ)² / (‖w₁²‖ ‖w₂²‖). It compares every harmonic of one connectome with every harmonic of the other, weighted by how much each prior trusts them, so it needs no harmonic matching and lets each connectome keep its own frequency scale; it equals 1 for identical priors. Depth weighting, the same for every connectome, was left out, and so was CSET, whose unweighted prior makes the measure 1 for any connectome. We compared the individual prior with the prior of each perturbed connectome and of each surrogate, and read each surrogate's equivalent perturbation off the perturbation curve by linear interpolation. Since the λ = 0 harmonic carries the largest weight (w = 1) but only reflects the dipoles' degrees, which edge swaps preserve, we computed the similarity twice: with every harmonic, and without the λ = 0 harmonics.

The two versions describe perturbation differently (@fig-annex-prior-sim). With every harmonic, the similarity fell from 1 to `{python} ps_all_10` at 10% perturbation and `{python} ps_all_30` at 30%, then levelled off at `{python} ps_all_100`. Without the λ = 0 harmonic, it stayed above `{python} ps_nz_40` up to 40% and only fell steeply afterwards, to `{python} ps_nz_70` at 70% and `{python} ps_nz_100` at 100%. The difference comes from the spectrum: random swaps add long-range shortcuts, which raise the smallest nonzero eigenvalue from `{python} ps_lambda_orig` in the individual connectome to `{python} ps_lambda_10` at 10% and `{python} ps_lambda_50` at 50%. The low-pass weights then switch off nearly every harmonic except λ = 0, whose share of the prior grew from `{python} ps_share_orig`% to `{python} ps_share_10`% at 10%, `{python} ps_share_30`% at 30% and `{python} ps_share_50`% at 50%. With every harmonic, the similarity therefore mostly tracks this collapse of the prior onto the λ = 0 harmonic, and its floor (`{python} ps_all_100`) is that harmonic's contribution alone. Without it, the similarity tracks how much the shapes of the remaining harmonics change, which happens later.

The surrogates fell into the same two groups in both versions. The atlas and both local surrogates were closest to the individual prior (similarity `{python} ps_close_all` with every harmonic, `{python} ps_close_nz` without λ = 0), and atlas-bin and GBF were further away (`{python} ps_far_all` and `{python} ps_far_nz`). Their equivalent perturbation, however, depended on the version: `{python} ps_close_all_eq`% for the close group and `{python} ps_far_all_eq`% for atlas-bin and GBF with every harmonic, against `{python} ps_close_nz_eq`% and `{python} ps_far_nz_eq`% without λ = 0. The graph surrogates keep a spectrum close to the individual one (`{python} ps_share_graph`% of the prior in the λ = 0 harmonic, against `{python} ps_share_orig`% for the individual connectome), so they score well when the spectral collapse dominates the measure, and less well when only the shapes of the harmonics count. GBF's λ = 0 harmonics, one constant per hemisphere, hold `{python} ps_share_gbf`% of its prior, which is why it gains the most when they are removed.

The equivalent perturbation is therefore only a rough bracket, between `{python} ps_eq_min`% and `{python} ps_eq_max`% depending on the surrogate and the version. In both versions, every surrogate falls well short of the `{python} ps_corr_end`% up to which wCSET kept its correlation advantage over sLORETA and dSPM in the perturbation experiment, and the close group falls within the range where wCSET was more accurate than sLORETA in localization (up to `{python} ps_loc_end`%). Atlas-bin and GBF fall within that range with every harmonic, but between `{python} ps_loc_end`% and `{python} ps_loc_worse`% without λ = 0, where wCSET was neither significantly better nor worse than sLORETA. The similarity compares priors, not reconstructions, so these equivalents locate the surrogates on the perturbation scale but do not predict their accuracy.

```{python filename="simf_prior_similarity_plot.py"}
#| echo: false

#| fig-cap: "Similarity between wCSET's prior built on the individual connectome and on perturbed or surrogate connectomes (cosine similarity of the prior covariance matrices; 1 = identical priors), (a) with every harmonic and (b) without the λ = 0 harmonics. Black line: perturbed connectomes versus the share of edges swapped. Colored dashed lines: surrogates; each ends at its equivalent perturbation (dot), read off the black line by linear interpolation."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.2), sharey=True)
titles = {ps_all: "a. Every harmonic", ps_nz: "b. Without the λ = 0 harmonics"}
for ax, col in zip(axes, PRIOR_SIM_VERSIONS):

    for s in surrogates_full:

    ax.set_title(titles[col], loc="left", fontsize=10)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Prior similarity to the individual connectome")
axes[0].set_ylim(0, 1.03)
axes[1].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8, frameon=False)
fig.tight_layout()
```

## Study III: Clinical Dynamics (Simultaneous iEEG/EEG) {#sec-annex-study3}

### wCSET reproduced the intracranial pattern better in one of two patients with cortical sources {#sec-annex-s3-correlation}

<!-- TODO: add the peak summaries for comparison with Grova et al. 2016 and Afnan et al. 2026: the signed spatial correlation averaged over the 5 samples centred on 2.0 s, where the spikes are aligned, and the AUC at that peak. The saved bootstrap (results/intra/bootstrap, *_peak and *_peak_boot) still centres the peak on the recorded iEEG's GFP maximum (2.065 s in Patient 2, 1.980 s in Patient 3), so it needs a full rerun before these are reported. -->

```{python filename="intra_window_full_stats.py"}
#| output: false
import mindmap as mm
from IPython.display import Markdown

# Same test as the main text (index.qmd, results_intra_vieeg_significance.py), for every patient and competitor: the
# window mean of the signed spatial correlation, wCSET vs. each competitor, paired bootstrap over bursts of spikes
# (processing_intra.qmd, "Spike-level bootstrap"), Holm across the 5 competitors, mean difference with its basic CI
# at CI_LEVEL (99%, as in the main text).
S3_SUBJECTS = ["48", "34", "12", "50"]
S3_PATIENTS = {"48": "1", "34": "2", "12": "3 (deep source)", "50": "4 (deep source)"}
S3_COMPETITORS = ["sloreta", "cset", "dspm", "wmne", "beltrami"]
S3_WINDOW = "correlation_spatial_signed_window"

s3_boot = mm.metric.MetricSuite.load("../results/intra/bootstrap")
s3_vs = {
    sub: s3_boot.stat.bootstrap(
        S3_WINDOW, group_by="Method", comparisons=s3_boot.stat.build_comparisons(["wcset"], S3_COMPETITORS),
        pairing_col="Subject", filters={"Subject": sub}, replicates=f"{S3_WINDOW}_boot", replicate_col="draw",
        estimator="mean_diff", correction="holm", ci_method="basic", ci_level=CI_LEVEL,
    ).vs("wcset")  # positive = wCSET better
    for sub in S3_SUBJECTS
}

def _s3_level(sub, method):
    return s3_boot.to_df(metrics=S3_WINDOW, filters={"Subject": sub, "Method": method})["Value"].item() + 0.0

# @tbl-annex-s3-window: one block per patient, wCSET first, then each competitor with its difference and p_corrected
_rows = []
for sub in S3_SUBJECTS:
    _rows.append([S3_PATIENTS[sub], METHOD_LABELS["wcset"], fmt_num(_s3_level(sub, "wcset"), 2), "", ""])
    for c in S3_COMPETITORS:
        v = s3_vs[sub].loc[c]
        _rows.append(["", METHOD_LABELS[c], fmt_num(round(_s3_level(sub, c), 2) + 0.0, 2),  # + 0.0: no "-0.00"
                      f"{v['mean_diff']:.2f} ({v['mean_diff_ci_low']:.2f} to {v['mean_diff_ci_high']:.2f})",
                      f"{v['p_corrected']:.3f}" + (" *" if v["significant"] else "")])
s3_table = "\n".join(
    [f"| Patient | Method | r (window mean) | wCSET − method ({CI_LEVEL * 100:g}% CI) | p_corrected |",
     "|:--|:--|--:|:--|--:|"] + ["| " + " | ".join(r_) + " |" for r_ in _rows])
s3_n_boot = f'{s3_boot.metadata["bootstrap"]["n_boot"]:,}'
```

This section reports the main text's Study III comparison in full: the signed spatial correlation between virtual and recorded iEEG, averaged over the comparison window, for every patient and method, with every difference from wCSET (@tbl-annex-s3-window). The tests are those of the main text: a paired bootstrap over bursts of spikes (`{python} s3_n_boot` draws), Holm-corrected across the five competitors within each patient, with Bonferroni-corrected 99% basic CIs. The main text quotes the ranges of these values. Patients 3 and 4 had deep sources, far from the cortical source space, so no method's virtual iEEG agreed with their recordings.

```{python filename="intra_window_full_table.py"}

#| label: tbl-annex-s3-window

Markdown(s3_table)
```
